name: wisbek
author: rule-family designer (world: clock times h:mm on a 12-hour clock)
description: CLOCK-TIME RULE-FAMILY class (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md; brainstorm in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_clock.md). CLUE = 2 or 3 example times on a 12-hour clock, one per line, written h:mm (1:00 .. 12:59), ALL WITH DIFFERENT HOURS. ANSWER = one more time obeying the hidden rule, well formed, and AT AN HOUR THAT IS NOT IN THE CLUE (well-formedness, visible in the clue itself because the examples never repeat an hour; it is what kills copy-an-example and every same-hour edit in one scorer clause). UNIVERSE U: 10 templates, 66 concrete rules over the 720 times. Readouts: h, m, the minute digit sum m//10+m%10, the hour digit sum (10/11/12 -> 1/2/3), and the offset (m-5h)%60 = how many clock numbers past the hour number the minute hand points. TEMPLATES: (0) the minute digits add up to n, n in 3..12; (1) the minutes are in the n times table, n in 7,8,11,12; (2) the minute hand points at an even / an odd number; (3) the minute hand points n numbers past the hour number, n in 0,1,2,4,5,6,7,8,10,11 (n=0 is "the hands point at the same number", n=6 "at opposite numbers"); (4) the hands make a square corner ((m-5h)%30==15, i.e. n=3 or 9 lumped into one rule); (5) the minutes are n times the hour, n in 1..4; (6) the hour and the minutes add up to n, n in 15,20,..,60; (7) all the digits add up to n, n in 7..16; (8) the minutes are n more than the hour, n in 5,10,..,45; (9) COMPETITOR, the minutes are in the n-tens, n in 0..5. A rule may be the HIDDEN one only if a random time satisfies it with probability <= 0.11 (that is what a player who answers at random scores): that leaves 58 eligible rules and puts the two loose times-table rules (7 and 8, density .15 and .133) plus all six minute-decade rules in U as COMPETITORS the generator has to kill - killing the decade rules is what forces the examples to spread across the minute-decades. Mean probability of the hidden rule under a random time: 0.048. U is an ANTICHAIN (brute-forced over all 720 times: no rule's satisfying set contains another's), otherwise positive examples could never separate them; that is why there is NO "it is n minutes past the hour" / "half past" / "quarter to" template (an exact minute sits inside the digit-sum, times-table and decade rules), why "the minutes are the same as the hour" excludes "the hour digits add up to the same as the minute digits" (it contains it), and why "the minute hand points at twice the hour number" is absent (twice an hour is always even, so it sits inside "points at an even number"). Also rejected as degenerate on a whole-minute clock: "the hands are exactly on top of each other" and "exactly opposite" and "exactly a right angle" are true at 12:00 and 6:00 and nowhere else, because 30h-5.5m is almost never 0, 180 or 90 for integer m - they are replaced by the exact clock-face versions in templates 3 and 4. GENERATE draws the TEMPLATE uniformly, then a parameter, then one example per hour from a set of distinct hours, keeping the set only if the examples together leave exactly one rule of U alive while no proper subset does (uniqueness + minimality), and only if at least 3 satisfying times remain at unused hours. Measured over 500 clues: 500/500 unique, 500/500 minimal, 500/500 all-distinct hours; 52% three examples, 48% two; template mix 38-69 of 500 each; mean 0.40 ms, max 1.0 ms; clue <= 17 chars; answer <= 5 chars. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (never in U, often consistent with the examples - learning what this class never says is the game; "fits" = consistent with every example, "scores" = a player who always answers with an instance of it at a fresh hour): "the minutes stay inside the range of minutes in the clue" fits 100% scores 8%; "the hour stays inside the range of hours in the clue" fits 100% scores 5%; "the minutes are bigger than the hour" fits 70% scores 4%; "it is in the same half of the hour as the examples" fits 51% scores 5%; "the minutes are all even / all odd" fits 42% scores 5%; "the minutes end in 0 or 5" fits 31% scores 10%; "the hour is odd / even" fits 26% scores 4%; "all the digits are different" fits 27% scores 4%; "the hour divides exactly into the minutes" fits 23% scores 8%; "both hands are in the same half of the face" fits 15% scores 5%; "it is o'clock / quarter past / half past / quarter to" fits 0.4% scores 10%. The class only ever makes TIGHT statements (the digits add up to exactly n, the minute hand is exactly n numbers past the hour, the minutes are exactly 3 times the hour) and never loose ones (at least, at most, bigger than, odd/even, morning/afternoon, between two o'clocks); the two 100%-consistent traps are the loose cousins of its own readouts. On average 4.9 excluded rules also fit every example, so a player whose universe is U plus the obvious extras faces ~5.9 survivors: picking one uniformly scores 26%, picking a wrong (excluded) one scores 8%. WITNESSES over 500 fresh clues: copy an example verbatim 0%; copy an example with one digit changed 9.6% (only 33% of such edits are even well formed - two thirds keep the hour); the same hour as an example with different minutes 0%; the same minutes as an example at a fresh hour 34.8% (the foothold - the cheap probe that needs the fresh-hour insight but not the rule); an example's minutes +/-1 at a fresh hour 2.6%; a random well-formed time 5.0%; a random time at any hour 3.6%; an instance of the commonest single U-rule (square corner) ignoring the clue 16.6%; a player who has mapped U perfectly 100%; a player who has mapped U minus its two rarest templates 84%; the true rule 100%. SOLVE re-derives the survivor exactly as the scorer does and returns a uniformly random valid time at a random unused hour (never canonical, never minimal). SCORE is 895 chars (needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it parses the example times, rebuilds all 66 rules of U, filters, insists on a single survivor and checks the answer. No hidden channel.

# --- world: a clock time "h:mm" on a 12-hour clock; 720 possible times -------------------
TIMES = [(h, m) for h in range(1, 13) for m in range(60)]

def HD(h):
    """digit sum of the hour: 1..9 -> h, 10/11/12 -> 1/2/3"""
    return h if h < 10 else h - 9

def MD(m):
    """digit sum of the two minute digits"""
    return m // 10 + m % 10

def P(r, t):
    """Is time t = (hour, minute) an example of rule r = (template, parameter)?"""
    k, n = r
    h, m = t
    if k < 1: return MD(m) == n                     # the minute digits add up to n
    if k < 2: return m % n == 0                     # the minutes are in the n times table
    if k < 3: return m % 5 == 0 and (m // 5) % 2 == n   # minute hand on an even/odd number
    if k < 4: return (m - 5 * h) % 60 == n          # minute hand n/5 numbers past the hour number
    if k < 5: return (m - 5 * h) % 30 == 15         # the hands make a square corner
    if k < 6: return m == n * h                     # the minutes are n times the hour
    if k < 7: return h + m == n                     # the hour and the minutes add up to n
    if k < 8: return HD(h) + MD(m) == n             # all the digits add up to n
    if k < 9: return m - h == n                     # the minutes are n more than the hour
    return m // 10 == n                             # COMPETITOR: the minutes are in the n-tens

# The universe U: 10 templates, 66 concrete rules.  Templates 0-8 may be the hidden rule
# (subject to the density ceiling below); template 9 is a competitor the generator must kill,
# which is what forces the examples to spread across the minute-decades.
U = ([(0, n) for n in range(3, 13)]
     + [(1, n) for n in (7, 8, 11, 12)]
     + [(2, 0), (2, 1)]
     + [(3, n) for n in (0, 5, 10, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50, 55)]
     + [(4, 0)]
     + [(5, n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
     + [(6, n) for n in range(15, 61, 5)]
     + [(7, n) for n in range(7, 17)]
     + [(8, n) for n in range(5, 50, 5)]
     + [(9, n) for n in range(6)])

# ---- tables built once per worker (~60 ms at module level, not charged to max_generate_ms) --
BIT = {}
for _k, _r in enumerate(U):
    BIT[_r] = 1 << _k
MASK = []
for _t in TIMES:
    _v = 0
    for _r in U:
        if P(_r, _t):
            _v |= BIT[_r]
    MASK.append(_v)
SATH = {}                       # rule -> {hour: [indices of satisfying times]}
DENS = {}                       # rule -> fraction of the 720 times that satisfy it
for _r in U:
    _d = {}
    for _i, _t in enumerate(TIMES):
        if MASK[_i] & BIT[_r]:
            _d.setdefault(_t[0], []).append(_i)
    SATH[_r] = _d
    DENS[_r] = sum(len(v) for v in _d.values()) / 720.0

# A rule may be the hidden one only if a random time satisfies it with probability <= 0.11 —
# that number is the score of a player who answers at random.  The two loose members of the
# times-table template (7 and 8) stay in U as competitors instead.
TEMPL = {}
for _r in U:
    if _r[0] != 9 and DENS[_r] <= 0.11:
        TEMPL.setdefault(_r[0], []).append(_r)
TKEYS = sorted(TEMPL)

def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(400):
        # template first, then a parameter, so no template is rare merely for owning fewer rules
        rule = r.choice(TEMPL[r.choice(TKEYS)])
        d = SATH[rule]
        hrs = list(d)
        b = BIT[rule]
        if len(hrs) < 4:
            continue
        best = None
        for size in (3, 2, 4):
            if len(hrs) < size + 1:
                continue
            for _t in range(200):
                # one example per hour, all hours different: the clue itself shows that the
                # hour is never the rule, and the answer must use an hour that is not there
                T = [r.choice(d[h]) for h in r.sample(hrs, size)]
                m = -1
                for i in T:
                    m &= MASK[i]
                if m != b:                       # the set must leave exactly this rule alive
                    continue
                ok = True
                for k in range(size):            # ... and no proper subset may
                    mm = -1
                    for i in T[:k] + T[k + 1:]:
                        mm &= MASK[i]
                    if mm.bit_count() == 1:
                        ok = False
                        break
                if ok:
                    best = T
                    break
            if best:
                break
        if best is None:
            continue
        used = set(TIMES[i][0] for i in best)
        # the answer must be buildable at some unused hour
        if sum(len(v) for h, v in d.items() if h not in used) < 3:
            continue
        return "\n".join("%d:%02d" % TIMES[i] for i in sorted(best, key=lambda i: TIMES[i]))
    return "2:14\n7:32\n10:50"

def solve(clue):
    E = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in (l.split(":") for l in clue.split())]
    U = ([(0, n) for n in range(3, 13)] + [(1, n) for n in (7, 8, 11, 12)] + [(2, 0), (2, 1)]
         + [(3, n) for n in (0, 5, 10, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50, 55)] + [(4, 0)]
         + [(5, n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)] + [(6, n) for n in range(15, 61, 5)]
         + [(7, n) for n in range(7, 17)] + [(8, n) for n in range(5, 50, 5)]
         + [(9, n) for n in range(6)])

    def p(r, t):
        k, n = r
        h, m = t
        u = m // 10 + m % 10
        if k < 1: return u == n
        if k < 2: return m % n == 0
        if k < 3: return m % 5 == 0 and (m // 5) % 2 == n
        if k < 4: return (m - 5 * h) % 60 == n
        if k < 5: return (m - 5 * h) % 30 == 15
        if k < 6: return m == n * h
        if k < 7: return h + m == n
        if k < 8: return (h if h < 10 else h - 9) + u == n
        if k < 9: return m - h == n
        return m // 10 == n

    V = [r for r in U if all(p(r, e) for e in E)]
    used = set(h for h, _ in E)
    C = [(h, m) for h in range(1, 13) if h not in used for m in range(60) if p(V[0], (h, m))]
    # a uniformly random valid time at a fresh hour - never the canonical or minimal one
    return "%d:%02d" % random.Random(clue).choice(C)
